title: Future with Will
tagline: decisions, offers and promises: will + base verb
why: We use will every day to offer help, make promises and decide things on the spot. Getting it right makes you sound friendly and natural.
know: I think, I'm sure, probably, I promise
able: make a quick decision, for example when you order food
mistakes: I will to phone you tonight.
Will you to join us for lunch?
I don't will forget your birthday.
A: This suitcase is so heavy! B: I'm going to help you.
A: This suitcase is so heavy! B: I'll help you.
use: Instant decisions, made while you speak: The phone's ringing. I'll get it.
Offers and promises: I'll carry that for you. I won't tell anyone.
Predictions from opinion, often with I think or probably: I think it'll be a good party.
form: I / you / he / she / we / they will work (short form: I'll, she'll, we'll)
I won't work = I will not work
Will you help me? What will you do?
signals: I think, I don't think, I'm sure, probably, maybe, I promise, I hope; reactions like Oh!, Wait, Don't worry
tip: Decided now, while speaking? Use will: I'll have the soup. Decided before? Use going to. And say I don't think he'll come, not I think he won't come.

pick.q: The phone's ringing. Stay there, I ___ get it.
pick.why: You decide at the moment of speaking, so use will: I'll get it.

pick.q: I promise I ___ you back on Friday.
pick.why: A promise uses will + base verb: I will pay. There is no 'to' after will.

pick.q: ___ you open the window, please? It's very hot in here.
pick.why: To ask someone to do something, use Will you + base verb: Will you open the window?

pick.q: Don't worry. I ___ tell anyone your secret.
pick.why: The negative of will is won't (will not). I won't tell anyone is a promise.

pick.q: I think the Blue Jays ___ the game tonight.
pick.why: After will, use the base verb with no -s: will win. This is a prediction from opinion (I think).

pick.q: I'm not sure, but I ___ be home late tonight.
pick.why: Probably usually goes after will: I will probably be late. Never 'am be' or 'will to'.

pick.q: My sister ___ like this restaurant. She hates fish.
pick.why: Negative prediction: won't + base verb. She won't like it.

pick.q: A: I can't open this jar. B: Give it to me. I ___ try.
pick.why: B offers to help at that moment, so use will: I'll try.

type.q: Sit down and relax. I ___ (make) you a cup of tea.
type.why: An offer made now: will + base verb. I'll make you a cup of tea.

type.q: Oh no, I forgot to email the landlord! I ___ (do) it right now.
type.why: You decide now, as you speak: I'll do it right now.

type.q: A: Can you call me tonight? B: Sure, I ___ (call) you after dinner.
type.why: Agreeing to a request is a promise: I'll call you after dinner.

type.q: Thanks for the loan. I promise I ___ (not / forget) to pay you back.
type.why: A promise in the negative: won't + base verb. I won't forget.

type.q: A: This shirt comes in red or blue. B: Hmm. I ___ (take) the blue one.
type.why: A quick decision in a shop: I'll take the blue one.

type.q: A: It's dark in here. B: Wait, I ___ (turn) on the light.
type.why: B decides at that moment, so use will: I'll turn on the light.

type.q: Those plates look heavy. I ___ (carry) some for you.
type.why: An offer of help made now: I'll carry some for you.

type.q: A: Coffee or tea? B: I ___ (have) a coffee, please.
type.why: When you order or choose on the spot, use will: I'll have a coffee.

spot.q: I will to send you the report this afternoon.
spot.why: After will, use the base verb with no 'to': I will send you the report.

spot.q: Will you to come to my birthday party on Saturday?
spot.why: Questions: Will + subject + base verb. Will you come? No 'to'.

spot.q: Don't worry, I don't will be late.
spot.why: The negative of will is won't, not don't will: I won't be late.

spot.q: That box looks heavy. I'm going to help you with it.
spot.why: An offer you decide on now uses will: I'll help you with it.

spot.q: I think it will rains this afternoon.
spot.why: After will, use the base verb with no -s: it will rain.

order.a: I will call you when I get home.
alt: When I get home I will call you.
order.why: Subject + will + base verb, then the time clause: I will call you when I get home.

order.a: Will you help me with my homework?
order.why: Questions start with Will, then the subject and the base verb: Will you help me?

order.a: I don't think she will come tonight.
order.why: We say I don't think + will for a negative opinion about the future.

order.a: We will probably arrive at about six.
alt: We probably will arrive at about six.
order.why: Probably usually goes after will: We will probably arrive.

pick.q: A: I've got a terrible headache. B: Sit down. I ___ get you some water.
pick.why: B decides to help at that moment, so use will: I'll get you some water.

pick.q: ___ you be at the meeting tomorrow morning?
pick.why: Will you + base verb: Will you be at the meeting? 'Do you be' and 'Are you be' are not English.

pick.q: Thank you so much for your help. I ___ forget it.
pick.why: Use will never + base verb. Only one negative word: I will never forget it.
After will, always the base verb: the bus will come.

pick.q: It's very late. I think I ___ a taxi home.
pick.why: A decision made now with I think: I think I'll take a taxi.

pick.q: My boss ___ be happy about this mistake.
pick.why: The negative of will is won't + base verb: My boss won't be happy.

type.q: A: I need a ride to the airport. B: No problem. I ___ (drive) you.
type.why: An offer made at that moment: I'll drive you.

type.q: A: So, the fish for you? B: Wait, I've changed my mind. I ___ (try) the chicken.
type.why: A choice made on the spot uses will: I'll try the chicken.

type.q: I promise I ___ (not / tell) your mother.
type.why: A negative promise: won't + base verb. I won't tell your mother.

type.q: A: This window is stuck. B: Let me see. I ___ (open) it for you.
type.why: An offer of help made now: I'll open it for you.

type.q: A: We're out of printer paper. B: Really? I ___ (order) some now.
type.why: B learns the news and decides now, so use will: I'll order some.

type.q: If you're cold, I ___ (lend) you my jacket.
type.why: An offer with if: will + base verb. I'll lend you my jacket.

type.q: A: My computer just crashed! B: Calm down. I ___ (have) a look at it.
type.why: An instant offer of help: I'll have a look at it.

type.q: A: I can't find my keys anywhere. B: I ___ (help) you look for them.
type.why: An offer made at that moment: I'll help you look.

spot.q: She will calls you back after lunch.
spot.why: After will, use the base verb with no -s, even with she: she will call.

spot.q: I'm sorry. I promise I not will do it again.
spot.why: The negative is won't (will not), and not comes after will: I won't do it again.

spot.q: A: There's no sugar. B: Oh, I go to the store and get some.
spot.why: B decides now, so use will, not the present simple: I'll go to the store.

spot.q: When will you to finish the report?
spot.why: Question word + will + subject + base verb: When will you finish? No 'to'.

order.a: I will text you after the meeting.
alt: After the meeting I will text you.
order.why: Subject + will + base verb + the rest: I will text you after the meeting.

order.a: Will they be at the party tonight?
order.why: Will comes first in a question, then the subject and the base verb.

order.a: I'm sure you will enjoy the film.
order.why: I'm sure + will for a prediction from opinion: you will enjoy the film.

bank.q: A: The baby's crying. B: Okay, I ___ go and see.
bank.why: B decides at that moment, so use will: I'll go and see.
Will + base verb: I hope you will feel better soon.

bank.q: ___ it be cold in Ottawa next week?
bank.why: A question about the future with be: Will it be cold?

bank.q: I'm really sorry. I ___ do it again.
bank.why: A promise about the future: won't + base verb. I won't do it again.

bank.q: We ___ probably need more chairs for the party.
bank.why: A prediction with probably: will probably + base verb.

bank.q: Don't touch that pan. You ___ burn your hand!
bank.why: A warning about the future: will + base verb. You will burn your hand.

bank.q: The new manager ___ start until March.
bank.why: Negative future: won't + base verb, with no 'to'. The new manager won't start until March.

bank.q: A: It's so hot in this car. B: I ___ turn on the air conditioning.
bank.why: B reacts and decides now, so use will: I'll turn it on.

bank.q: A: I left my wallet at home. B: Don't worry. I ___ (pay) for lunch today.
bank.why: An offer made on the spot: I'll pay for lunch.

bank.q: Wait for me here. I promise I ___ (not / be) long.
bank.why: A promise in the negative: I won't be long.

bank.q: A: Someone's at the door. B: I ___ (get) it.
bank.why: A decision made at that moment: I'll get it.

bank.q: A: This soup needs salt. B: Here, I ___ (pass) it to you.
bank.why: An offer of help made now: I'll pass it to you.
A big request about the future: Will you marry me?

bank.q: I will to bring the salad to the picnic.
bank.why: No 'to' after will: I will bring the salad.

bank.q: I don't think it will snow this weekend.
bank.why: This sentence is correct. I don't think + will is the natural way to say a negative opinion.

bank.q: Will you can help me tomorrow?
bank.why: Never put will and can together. Say Will you help me? (or Can you help me?).

bank.q: That bag looks heavy. I'll carry it for you.
bank.why: This sentence is correct. An offer made on the spot uses will: I'll carry it.

bank.a: I will see you at the station tomorrow.
alt: I will see you tomorrow at the station.
Tomorrow I will see you at the station.
bank.why: Subject + will + base verb + place + time: I will see you at the station tomorrow.

bank.a: What time will you be home tonight?
bank.why: Question word + will + subject + base verb: What time will you be home?

bank.a: I think it will be a busy day.
bank.why: I think + will for a prediction from opinion: it will be a busy day.
